scope: Source discovery and one bounded document capture only. No calendar knowledge ledger, candidate feature, market-data/return read, fit, account replay or model change.
owner_authorization: Root explicitly authorized at most 12 official rule/announcement documents for read-only discovery and small source capture. Future native source-intake/ledger execution remains separately controlled by the source plan and its review.

capture_boundary.reuse_rule: The eight successful bytes are discovery cache, not a newly authorized ledger. A later authorized workflow should verify their SHA and reuse them rather than redownload. The four SEC documents are web-tool-readable but lack native raw-byte capture; do not fabricate hashes or claim Recorder archival.

publication_contract.date_source: Document body or the official associated release, never search-engine publication/crawl dates, HTTP Last-Modified or current access time.
publication_contract.proposed_conservative_available_from: Following local midnight after the stated publication day, America/New_York, unless a separately reviewed exact timestamp exists. This is a date-precision research convention, not a measured receipt timestamp or original-vintage proof.
publication_contract.same_day_use: Not allowed by these date-only sources at 09:29/09:46.
publication_contract.effective_vs_knowledge: Rule filing/effectiveness is recorded separately and does not backdate public knowledge.
publication_contract.current_snapshot_limitation: The captured pages are current accessible representations with historical body datelines; none is represented as a contemporaneously archived immutable vintage.

qualification_gaps: Pre-2011 complete NYSE/NYSE Arca ordinary-holiday and observed-day rules were not established. The 2010 Rule51 documents provide interruption authority and hours, not the missing Rule51.10 holiday text.

The three selected annual schedules directly cover only 2015-2016, 2021-2023 and 2026-2028. Complete prior-known ordinary schedules for 2011-2014 and 2017-2020 remain unknown. 2024-2025 may only be addressed later from an explicitly reviewed continuing-rule interpretation; this inventory has not approved that extrapolation.

The general month/year-end observation exception is discretionary. Specific announced New Year dates support their named years; a universal Saturday-New-Year algorithm has not been independently established here.
Nasdaq extraordinary-closure notices prove Nasdaq venue scope only. Separate NYSE/NYSE Arca matching event notices or a justified receiving-calendar mapping are absent from this finite corpus.
Four SEC PDFs returned HTTP403 in the single native capture attempt. Web-tool body inspection establishes readable content, not a locally captured original-byte SHA or durable Recorder evidence.
All selected publication evidence is day-precision; true first-publication timestamps and historical page immutability are unverified.
No claim is made that this finite corpus exhausts all extraordinary closures, all later rule amendments, or all venue changes in 2011-2026.
qualitative_boundary_notes: Sandy closures concern the end of October; their staged announcement and reopening sequence can matter to expected-last knowledge. No TOM values or realized classifications were calculated.
The Bush closure is near the opening of December and can affect first-three counting. The late-day publication uncertainty is preserved.

Carter's January 9 closure and Juneteenth's June 19/observed dates appear away from the first/last boundary under an otherwise normal schedule. This is qualitative calendar position, not a feature calculation or exemption from recording the events.
Failure to qualify the complete source ledger is a data-coverage result, not evidence for or against the TOM return hypothesis.
